Excavated a small portion of the plaster and found the cable exactly where I expected it. A few more mini excavations and I found the fault. 1. Buy or Do Not Buy?,Buy It.,2. What is so good about this?,It is a unique toy, so much fun. It’s a mini helicopter/drone, but packs quite a punch. It is affordable, and so worth the entertainment you receive in return. The basic idea is it floats up in the air like a helicopter, and comes down. Your job is to position an object or your hand under the toy as it drops to trigger it to fly straight back up again, the longer your hand/object is placed under the toy, the higher the toy will rise. The toy lights up beautifully, which makes playing in the dark super fun, inside or outside.,3. How do you play with it?,Don’t make the mistake I made, and not read the instructions. Actually, I still haven’t read it 😊, and figure out how to play with it correctly by purely by accident, albeit after several knocks and falls…of the toy, not me. Turn on the toy by pressing the black rubber button at the bottom of the toy. Hold the toy on your hand upright, press the button on the remote to turn on the blades, then let it go. No need to push it up…just let it go. As it floats up and comes down, just place your hand under the toy to make it rise again.,To avoid potentially damaging the toy, know that there is a sensor under the body (ball) of the toy. The longer your hand or any object is under the sensor, the higher the toy will rise. So, when you get started playing with the toy, and wonder like I did, why it keeps going up and being stuck on the ceiling, you are probably placing your hand under the sensor for too long. No worries, if you are too short to grab the toy as it floats under the ceiling, just press the button again, and after a couple of seconds, you will notice the blades slow down and the toy drop, just press the button again to make it rise again to avoid hitting the floor.,4. How much of playtime do you get with it?,About 10 minutes. I charge it for about 20 minutes, and have been getting about 10 minutes of continuous play time. Given the size of the toy, I think this is probably as long as the charge can hold.,5. Is it safe?,I think so. The blades are plastic, and flexible. They are not hard. As long as you play it the right away, you should not hurt yourself. Also, the fact that it floats up means that it will rise anytime something is under it, so the chances of it hitting your eyes or injuring you otherwise is small as long as you are not throwing it horizontally. The ball/base is clear plastic. It is not heavy or metal-like, so no danger there. Small kids should play under adult supervision.

Though we have some large TVs in our basement and upstairs that are connected to sound receivers and which pump out all the sound we could ever need there, we were in need of something a bit more compact, yet powerful for the 32 inch TV we have on our main floor. Having been impressed with TaoTronic's various personal tech offerings (we own a ton of their products after discovering them through Amazon), we decided to take a chance on their 32 inch soundbar offering and are happy we did! It combines excellent sound with, a compact footprint and easy configuration.,The soundbar is quite compact, and really puts the "bar" in soundbar. We have it sitting on the sill above our fireplace, but it comes prepared to be easily mounted in other configurations with mount kits. We have connected it via optical cable to our TV, an extremely important feature we are glad appears on the bar - optical output allows for *zero loss* in fidelity as the signal is transmitted by light, rather than a soundwave which is subject to degredation. To provide perspective, optical in/output is what audio purists will not do without in their HiFi systems.,We enjoy the other connectivity options (which include bluetooth and an auxiliary input), though admittedly, we do not make much use of them, especially the RCA output, which I imagine would be useful for folks with older TVs that don't have any other type of audio interface (upgrade your TV, for god's sake, if RCA is all you have!!!). I've attached a chromecast audio to the soundbar, which has allowed it to become part of the larger audio setup in our house (to the extent, you don't know what a chromecast audio is, I strongly suggest you look into it - though discontinued, they are one of the most versatile devices ever created to make regular speakers "smart").,The speaker has several presets to account for movies, gaming and otherwise, but we find that the standard preset is itself more than enough for us. The audio can get impressively loud without any distortion - should we have a "rave" or a super intense movie night in our house, we would probably opt for the basement due to the comfort of a big sofa, but are comforted by the fact that this soundbar could easily belt out all the sound we needed.,There is one area for improvement, though it doesn't detract from the overall review of the product, is that, while the soundbar is accessible via a provided remote-control, it isn't configurable to work with a Roku remote. I think TaoTronics would do well to submit the product to Roku such that it can be configured to work with Roku's remote, as many TVs can now be done. Again, not a huge quibble, but just a thought.,Overall, we are really happy with this TaoTronics soundbar. Based on the items we've purchased from them, the company's goal seems to be to produce budget versions of high-end products that actually perform well enough for their price-point, that the value proposition is hard to beat. This is yet again the case here.

review_title: Good looks, good sound quality, good price, great product!
review_text: My girlfriend recently moved into a new apartment, and we wanted to pick up a soundbar to go with her TV so she didn't have to use only TV audio to watch her shows and movies and stuff.  Obviously, for a grad student, price is still important, and I found this soundbar.,The packaging and shipping of this product was good enough to keep it from being damaged in the mail, about what you'd expect.  After opening it, I was surprised at the fit and finish.  Overall, the soundbar looks great and of high quality.  The buttons on it are nice and clicky and the front display looks really nice with the LEDs and indicators shining through the front grille.  I don't think there is an option to turn off the lights but I didn't really find them distracting.,Sound quality in this unit is great!  Obviously, this comes with a caveat.  The price of speaker systems often determines the sound quality, and in this case, it isn't too much above the bar that I set for it.  I expected decently punchy low end, clear voice, and a decent high end.  What we got was a little bit lacking in the bass department, good voices, clear midtones, and a bit of a cut on the high end.  Either way, the sound output of this soundbar is better than the 43" TCL tv that it's paired with.  The stereo separation on the soundbar is pretty good, and while it doesn't fully simulate having  surround sound system, it does well for what it is.  There are several sound modes on the speaker, and they definitely make a difference in what the output sound is like, I would definitely use each mode for what it says; for example, movie mode makes music sound kinda weird, so you should use music mode for music.  I think music mode boosts the bass response, the movie mode boosts midtones and voice registry, and I don't really know what the game mode does.,I never expected this device to hold a candle to my full theater 7.2.2 setup at home, but it does well enough for a small sound bar at $68 bucks.,The amount of ports on the soundbar is good, but not outstanding.  It's nice that a toslink optical cable was provided, that's what I'm using to power it, and that an RCA to 3.5mm was provided as well.  I tried out the Bluetooth mode as well, and it plays music perfectly fine.  Didn't get a chance to test out the latency yet but it's probably just average.,We have the soundbar just sitting on the TV stand but they actually provide drywall anchors as well if you want to mount it to the wall.  The power cord isn't super long but it is probably enough to get to the closest outlet near the TV.,Overall I'm pretty pleased with the performance of this sound bar, and while it can't touch the sound of a real surround system or a more expensive Bose or other name brand system, it hits a mark above what you'd expect and is more than enough to get better sound that your TV's system.

I sent him off into the night with some graham crackers and a prayer. I hope he finds another safe place to squat.,Edit: I have caught 5 mice in 24 hours. The traps are still set and they are easy to empty no touch. My husband just goes far up in the woods and releases them. Win Win, they are out of the house and they get to live. Very pleased with this purchase.

It's only a small amount to pay for never ending use (I know a LOT of people who buy traps that kill because they are cheap....),This is 100% easy to use, and understand. Set up was a breeze, trapping 100% it did not simply go off unless there was a mouse trapped inside. (Which....apparently there was some mouse breeding in my house as of lately bc I caught multiple small mice who didnt appear fully grown.) Simply set up, put in a place you would see prior activity (droppings or noises etc) kitchens are mainly the area to look in - and I used a couple pieces of cereal as my "bait" you can use whatever youd like that gives off a scent to lure in the mouse. (My mom uses peanut butter but that's kinda messy),Catch your mouse, release mouse easily by the pull off end and say bye!!,Releasing the mouse in an area not close to your home is important! We released any we caught about a 1/2 mile away where there seems to be a lot of land and woods and they can find new shelter elsewhere.,Please, get this if you are having some friends come and trying to crash in your home....it takes a little time to set up and release but not a lot - and you dont have to live with the guilt of killing an innocent furry baby because you simply dont want to harbor the pests - you will feel good about yourself. I finally broke down and bought a microscope after inadvertently wiping the serial number off a microchip while scrubbing at conformal covering over a PCB - that serial is just painted on and my 99.9% isopropyl wiped it right out like BAM! The polymer coating didn't even slow it down. All my other magnifiers are less-than perfect in best cases, and just plain useless here. I knew there had to be microns of paint left but I needed more magnification. I still didn't expect to get better than a vague idea of what the printed characters might have been with any grade microscope.,This thing exceeded my expectations in the first 10 seconds of use. Unlike another microscope I have (a little handheld deal), this magnifies clear down to 10x - typically when it says "micro" on it the thing wants to start at 60x or 100x. I read it in the product promo material and honestly didn't believe it'd go that low - figured it had to be a mistake. Between a legitimate 10x magnification, an absolutely phenomenal LED lighting package (that floods the item directly under the lens with white light), and an adjustable material-bench, I was able to get a crystal clear image of the otherwise scattered flecks of paint left on the IC in question. I believe the built-in lighting package helped immensely - I seriously get an enhanced image that's as clear as it would have been when the paint was fresh. The LCD display quality is unbelievable too.

Multi-purpose:,I am really impressed with this product. It is dual purpose. You can also use this as a sleep mask – great for traveling.,Set-up:,Manufacturer recommends charging it up for two hours before first use. I charged it up overnight the first time. USB charger comes built in to the headband. The cord is not conspicuous or bothersome when you’re wearing the headphone. They also supply a small extension USB charge. Set up was super easy. You press the play button for about three seconds to pair with to your phone’s Bluetooth. If it’s attempting to paid, menu console light up blue-red. It took about 5 seconds for my phone to recognize the headband. The headband will show up as “BT-FAAH” in your phone’s list of Bluetooth devices.,Functionality:,The ear pieces are movable, so you can move them forward and back to align them perfectly to your ears. The + - buttons are dual purpose. If you press them once, they skip and rewind your playlist. If you press and hold them, they control volume. If you press the play button for three seconds, you will hear “power off” and it will turn off. If you press the play button again for three seconds, you will hear “power on,” then “connected.” Press the play button again and you can continue jamming from where you left off.,Quality, range, and performance:,The fabric is soft, stretchy, and light. Audio quality is very good, comparable to most brand name in-ear headphones. Range is solid. I placed my phone in a closet with obstructions around and walked away a distance of about 30 yards. The audio quality held up and I didn’t experience signal break or hear static noises, so the signal strength is really solid, and can probably extend much beyond 30 yards. I did several trials with and without obstructions around my phone, and the performance was consistent. In my experience, the battery lasts for about 18 hours of continuous use.
